title: Structure and Emission Properties of Er3Q9 (Q = 8-Quinolinolate)

material_class.structural_family: trinuclear 8-quinolinolate cluster with distorted square-antiprismatic ErN/O8 coordination

synthesis.procedure: A few drops of 28% aqueous NH3 were added to a mixture of 8-hydroxyquinoline (HQ; 0.157 g, 1.08 mmol) in H2O (100 mL) under mixing. After 30 min, an aqueous solution of Er(NO3)3·5H2O (0.160 g, 0.361 mmol) was added and the mixture was allowed to react for 2 days. A yellow precipitate formed, was collected by filtration, washed with water, 0.1 M NaOH, and water, and dried in an oven. Analytical results agreed with the ErQ3·H2O formulation. This solid was dissolved in hot CH3CN, the solvent was rotary evaporated to incipient precipitation, and yellow crystals of Er3Q9·CH3CN were obtained (yield 46%). IR spectra of the products before and after crystallization were superimposable except for water peaks.
synthesis.temperature: hot CH3CN used for recrystallization; reaction temperature not specified
synthesis.time: 30 min after NH3 addition, then 2 days after adding the Er salt
synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous precipitation followed by recrystallization from hot acetonitrile with rotary evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Yellow precipitate collected by filtration, washed with water, 0.1 M NaOH, and water, and oven-dried; dissolved in hot CH3CN and concentrated to incipient precipitation to give yellow crystals of Er3Q9·CH3CN.

properties.summary: Water-free trinuclear Er3Q9 shows Er(III) 4I15/2–4I13/2 absorption/emission near 1.52 μm (stronger PL band at 1530 nm) with Stark splitting. Intrinsic Er PL decay is 2.2 μs (build-up in a few ns; nearly single-exponential), attributed solely to resonant energy transfer to ligand aromatic C–H vibrations (DR overtone near 1680 nm; ν = 3047 cm−1); no O–H absorbance is detected. Similar PL lifetime is observed in 1.0×10−3 M nondeuterated DMSO. Förster modeling gives ~2 μs Er-to-C–H transfer and ~10 ns Er–Er migration.
